events/joint-declaration-justification-1: Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification

On Reformation Day 1999 the Lutheran World Federation and the Catholic Church signed a declaration stating a 'consensus in basic truths' on justification — by grace alone, through faith, not because of any merit — and that the 16th-century condemnations do not apply to the teaching it presents. Methodists (2006), Reformed (2017) and Anglicans (2016/17) later associated themselves.
Critiques from confessional Lutherans and some Catholics
events/kitzmiller-v-dover-2005/title: Kitzmiller v. Dover ruling on intelligent design
events/kitzmiller-v-dover-2005/summary: On 20 December 2005 a U.S. federal judge ruled that a Pennsylvania school board’s policy of introducing intelligent design in biology classes violated the Establishment Clause, finding ID to be a form of creationism rather than science. Michael Behe testified for the defence.
events/kitzmiller-v-dover-2005/causes/0: Intelligent design movement’s “teach the controversy” strategy
events/kitzmiller-v-dover-2005/consequen: Effectively ended ID in U.S. public-school science curricula
ID proponents disputed the ruling’s characterisation of their work
events/summorum-pontificum-2007/summary: Benedict XVI declares the 1962 Missal an "extraordinary form" of the one Roman Rite that any priest may celebrate without the bishop’s permission (7 July 2007).
events/acna-founded-2009/title: Formation of the Anglican Church in North America
events/acna-founded-2009/summary: At an assembly in Bedford, Texas, in June 2009, dioceses and congregations that had left the Episcopal Church and the Anglican Church of Canada, together with older continuing bodies such as the Reformed Episcopal Church, formed the Anglican Church in North America under Archbishop Robert Duncan.
events/acna-founded-2009/causes/0: Consecration of a partnered gay bishop (2003) and same-sex blessings
events/acna-founded-2009/consequences/0: ACNA recognised by GAFCON primates but not a member of the Anglican Communion's formal structures
events/acna-founded-2009/consequences/1: Extensive property litigation with the Episcopal Church
events/pope-francis-elected-2013/title: Election of Pope Francis, first Latin American pope
events/pope-francis-elected-2013/summary: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, Jesuit archbishop of Buenos Aires, was elected pope on 13 March 2013, the first from the Americas and the global South. His emphasis on mercy, the poor, the environment (Laudato si', 2015) and synodality reflected the shift of Catholicism's centre of gravity southward.
events/pope-francis-elected-2013/causes/: Growth of Catholicism in the global South
events/pope-francis-elected-2013/consequ: Debates between progressive and traditionalist Catholics
events/isis-expulsion-mosul-2014/title: Christians expelled from Mosul and the Nineveh Plains
events/isis-expulsion-mosul-2014/summary: In July–August 2014 the so-called Islamic State ordered Christians in Mosul to convert, pay jizya or leave, and then overran the Nineveh Plains, driving out some 120,000 Chaldean, Syriac and Assyrian Christians. It accelerated the collapse of Iraq's Christian population from over a million before 2003.
events/isis-expulsion-mosul-2014/consequ: Near-extinction of ancient Christian communities in Iraq and Syria
events/pan-orthodox-council-crete-2016/t: Holy and Great Council of Crete
events/pan-orthodox-council-crete-2016/s: After decades of preparation, ten autocephalous Orthodox churches met under Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew at Kolymbari. The churches of Russia, Antioch, Georgia and Bulgaria withdrew shortly before, exposing tensions over primacy within Orthodoxy.
events/pan-orthodox-council-crete-2016/c: Documents on mission, diaspora, marriage and relations with other Christians
events/umc-separation-2019/summary: The special General Conference (February 2019) narrowly adopts the "Traditional Plan" strengthening bans on same-sex weddings and LGBTQ clergy; between 2019 and 2023 some 7,600 US congregations (about a quarter) disaffiliate, many joining the Global Methodist Church (launched 2022). The 2024 General Conference removes the bans and approves regionalisation; several African conferences later leave.
events/umc-separation-2019/causes/0: Decades of debate since 1972 "incompatible with Christian teaching" clause
events/ukrainian-autocephaly-2019/title: Autocephaly of the Orthodox Church of Ukraine
events/ukrainian-autocephaly-2019/summar: The Ecumenical Patriarchate granted a tomos of autocephaly to the newly united Orthodox Church of Ukraine in January 2019. The Moscow Patriarchate broke communion with Constantinople, deepening a schism within world Orthodoxy that worsened after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
events/traditionis-custodes-2021/summary: Pope Francis (16 July 2021) revokes Benedict XVI’s provisions and declares the liturgical books promulgated after Vatican II the "unique expression" of the Roman Rite, restricting the older Mass to bishops’ permission in order to protect unity and acceptance of the Council.
events/traditionis-custodes-2021/causes/: Concerns about rejection of Vatican II
events/traditionis-custodes-2021/consequ: Further restrictions by the Dicastery for Divine Worship (2021, 2023)
events/fiducia-supplicans-2023/summary: A declaration of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith (18 December 2023), approved by Pope Francis, permits brief, spontaneous, non-liturgical blessings of couples in irregular situations, including same-sex couples, while reaffirming that marriage is between a man and a woman and that such blessings do not validate the union. Many African bishops’ conferences declined to implement it.
events/asbury-revival-2023/summary: After a routine chapel service on 8 February 2023 at Asbury University, students remained to pray, sing and confess for about two weeks of continuous worship that drew an estimated 50,000 visitors. Leaders deliberately avoided celebrity preachers; observers debated whether it constituted 'revival' and how much social media amplified it.
events/asbury-revival-2023/consequences/: Discussion of revival in a digital age
